note: Twenty-six pages, 50 measured regions but only 48 distinct page-plus-bbox keys, because p15 places two overlapping copies of one plot area at the identical box twice. Twenty-five of the regions are the page-foot WeChat stamp standing alone at the identical [448.3,721.7,583.1,789.1] block of exactly 693 paths and 0.0187 area on every page but one; on p10 the stamp is fused into the System B table's head and the pass reports a single 826-path region for both, the paper's one failure to separate furniture from content. The remaining regions hold sixteen exhibits - Figures 1 to 13 and Tables 1 to 3, both series complete with no gap - plus three table continuations and four duplicated raster placements. Two tables run across a page break and both are captioned under their LOWER half, so the measured Table 1 and Table 2 rows are the continuations. Caption side is therefore below on all sixteen rows, tables included, inverting the previous paper's kind-driven split. Table grids are drawn as sub-point black fills rather than strokes (Table 1 67+120 fills, zero lines; Table 2 133 black fills inside its fused region), while Table 3 is a 137x152 dpi bitmap with no rules at all and a coloured header instead. Resolution spans 109 dpi (Figure 2) to 220 dpi (Figure 12), but the softest art is the newest: Figure 6's plot area and Figure 9's legend bullets are pasted at 72 dpi. Citation is the thinnest of the block - two numbered pointers in the whole paper, 14 of 16 exhibits never named by number. Families: 5 flowchart-or-schematic, 3 bar, 2 line grids of four panels, 1 line, 1 scatter, 1 radar recorded as 'other', plus 3 table-grids. A printed caption has swallowed the next sentence's first word (Figure 3), and the text layer splits that word across the line break.
rules: All sixteen exhibits are captioned and numbered Figure 1 to Figure 13 and Table 1 to Table 3 with no gaps, so this is the first paper in the block with a clean numbering run in both series and no unnumbered apparatus row: sixteen exhibits, 50 measured regions, and the surplus is page stamps, table continuations and duplicated plot areas rather than missing numbers. [caption.verbatim] carries the number for every row.

Caption punctuation is uniform and unpunctuated - 'Figure N' and 'Table N' with no full stop and no colon on all sixteen rows, where the previous paper in the block printed a full stop on twenty of twenty-one - so [caption.numbering] reads 'Figure N' or 'Table N' sixteen times and no punctuation variant exists to report.

In this paper the table captions print BELOW their tables, not above: Table 1 at y 469.6 against a region ending y 463.1, Table 2 at y 219.6 against y 213.1, Table 3 at y 519.8 against y 493.7. [caption.position] is therefore 'below' for all sixteen rows, figures and tables alike, and a rule that infers kind from caption side would misclassify all three tables here.

Figure captions sit tight to their art: the gaps run from 6.5 pt (Figure 1) to 40.7 pt (Figure 5, whose Panel B axis intervenes), with ten of the thirteen inside 6.5-7.2 pt, while Table 3's caption clears its raster by 26.1 pt. [place.area_frac] and the caption gap do not covary - the loosest figure caption in the paper belongs to the tightest art block, not the largest.

Two exhibit texts are welded to their neighbours: Figure 3's caption ends '...industry performance: coverage' and the following sentence begins 'is the cornerstone of fairness', so the caption swallowed the next sentence's subject and the text layer splits the word as 'covera' + 'e'; Figure 7's raw line carries the watermark run after the caption. [caption.verbatim] for Figure 3 is therefore cut at 'covera' rather than repaired to 'coverage'.

Every table in this paper draws its grid as FILLS, not strokes: Table 1 is 67 black fills on its p8 part and 120 on its p9 part with no thin line anywhere, and Table 2's p10 part is 133 black fills inside a region whose other 693 paths are the stamp. [table.rule_style] 'boxed' for both rests on the fills enclosing every cell, so a stroke-only classifier reads 'no-rules' off a fully ruled table.

Table 3 inverts that: it is a bitmap with no rules whatsoever and no row banding, readable only through three coloured header cells, and it is the one table in the paper whose [table.rule_style] is 'no-rules' while the print is perfectly legible. Rules drawn as fills and a table drawn as a bitmap are opposite failures of the same classifier, and both occur here.

Two tables continue across a page break and both are captioned under their LOWER half, so the measured region of Table 1 and Table 2 is the continuation and the head is excluded: Table 1 splits 3 rows (p8) + 7 rows (p9) and Table 2 splits 8 rows (p10) + 3 rows (p11), and Table 2's Efficiency group label falls on the far side of the break from the rows it governs. [table.continued] is true for both, and [table.rows] counts the whole table, not the measured part.

The page stamp is fused into an exhibit exactly once: on p10 the table's right edge overlaps the stamp's x-range and the layout pass reports one 826-path region instead of two, so 25 of the 26 pages carry the stamp standalone at [448.3,721.7,583.1,789.1] and p10 carries it inside Table 2's head. [place.area_frac] 0.6708 on that region is a union of two different objects.

Region identity is not injective on p15: four raster placements collapse onto two page-plus-bbox keys, so the paper has 50 regions but 48 distinct keys, and the census records 48 measured regions. [place.solo_page] and any count keyed on regions must be read against the key count, not the region count.

Caption citation is the thinnest yet: exactly two numbered pointers in the whole paper - 'shown in Table 1' on p8 and 'according to the trend of the Figure 11' on p19 - so 14 of the 16 exhibits are never named by number, and every other exhibit reference is deictic ('the figure below', 'the right figure'). [mention.count] is 1 on those two rows and 0 on the other fourteen.

Figure 5's two panels print 29 category bars - twenty of the model's twenty-one countries, eight countries that are not in the model, and a printed 'Average' row - and the country that is missing is the United Kingdom, so the one exhibit that visualises the ability variable draws a different sample from the one the paper defines two pages later. Figures 6, 9 and 13 all print the same 21 labels including the United Kingdom, so this is one chart's defect and not a house convention; [geometry.printed_numbers] true does not imply the printed categories match the caption's data.

Families in this paper are mostly diagrams, not charts: five of the thirteen figures are flowcharts, schematics or timelines (F1, F2, F3, F4, F12), two are titled multi-panel line grids (F7, F8), three are bar charts (F5, F6, F9), one is a radar (F10, recorded as 'other' because the vocabulary has no radar family), one is a line (F11) and one a scatter (F13). [geometry.family] 'other' is used once and carries an explicit other_note.

Raster is again the default but at both extremes: seven exhibits are single bitmaps between 109 dpi (Figure 2) and 220 dpi (Figure 12), three figures are vector-only (F5, F9, F11), and two - F6 and F9's legend - paste their plot area at 72 dpi, one pixel per point, so the lowest-resolution marks in the paper are not its oldest scans but its most recent pastes. [geometry.printed_numbers] stays true wherever an axis exists, false on the five schematics.

tables.note: A four-column grid - first-level indicator, abbreviation of secondary indicators, secondary indicators, data processing - split across p8 and p9: the header row and the first three data rows (pcy, rmu, grc) sit at the foot of p8, the remaining seven (pfe, pou, ad-a, ad-b, ad-c, ad-d, dgr) at the head of p9, where the measured region is. Ten data rows under one header row, and the first column merges over three groups (Coverage 3, Fairness 2, Achievement 5), so [table.merged_cells] true. Every rule - the outer box, the column separators and every row line - is a fill of sub-point height rather than a stroke: 67 black fills on the p8 part and 120 on the p9 part, and not one thin line. The caption prints BELOW the closing rule, which inverts the usual table convention and is the reason the anchor region is the lower half of the table.

tables.note: A table that is a bitmap: 474x605 px at 137x152 dpi, so the raster is stretched 11 per cent vertically after it was pasted and the type inside it is the softest in the paper. Three columns - country, distance to the optimal solution, rank - and twenty-one data rows ranked 1 (Slovak Republic 0.639816) to 21 (Israel 0.264504), matching the prose on the same page. There are no rules at all: the grid is carried by three coloured header cells (beige, teal, orange) and by nothing else, so [table.rule_style] is 'no-rules' for a table that reads perfectly well, and the body is not banded. Width is half the text block - it sits in the right column with the prose running down its left side.
